input: Set up a telescope for backyard stargazing nights

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether this means physically assembling a new telescope, optimising an existing one, or building a full stargazing station changes everything about the plan.
A solo hobbyist needs different guidance than someone setting up for a family with young children or a small group, affecting how to explain steps and what to prioritise.
The backyard's light pollution level, horizon obstructions, and typical weather dramatically affect alignment method, equipment choices, and viewing targets.
Budget determines whether accessories like eyepieces, star charts, red-light torches, or a motorised mount are realistic additions to the plan.
Knowing the telescope type (refractor, reflector, Dobsonian, etc.) and whether it is already owned or yet to be purchased dictates the exact setup steps.
Targets of interest — planets, deep-sky objects, the Moon — shape which eyepieces to use, how to align, and which nights to plan sessions.
Knowing what a successful first session looks like — e.g., seeing a planet clearly, finding a specific object — sets the benchmark for whether the setup is working well.

gold.taskTitle: Set up telescope for backyard stargazing nights
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to set up a telescope in their backyard for regular nighttime stargazing sessions.

questions.title: Do you have a telescope already, or need to buy one?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan starts with a purchase guide or jumps straight to assembly and setup instructions.

questions.title: What type of objects most interest you to observe?
questions.description: Identifies whether the user wants to view the Moon, planets, deep-sky objects, or everything, shaping alignment method and eyepiece recommendations.

questions.title: Who will be using the telescope during sessions?
questions.description: Clarifies whether this is solo use, family-friendly, or for a group, affecting how detailed and accessible the setup instructions need to be.

questions.title: How much light pollution does your backyard have?
questions.description: The level of light pollution determines realistic viewing targets, necessary accessories, and whether a dark-sky trip should supplement backyard sessions.

questions.title: Does your setup budget include accessories beyond the telescope?
questions.description: Establishes whether the plan can include extras like additional eyepieces, a motorised mount, a red-light torch, or star-chart apps.

questions.title: Should this cover a one-time setup or a repeatable nightly routine?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan is a single assembly guide or a repeatable checklist for packing, aligning, and storing equipment each session.

questions.title: What does a successful first stargazing session look like to you?
questions.description: Defines the concrete success benchmark — e.g., clearly viewing Saturn's rings, finding a star cluster — so the plan can be optimised toward that outcome.
